newsitem.title: UK: Spain's 2 bln Ecu-euro bond due this week - traders.
newsitem.headline: Spain's 2 bln Ecu-euro bond due this week - traders.

text.p: Spain's forthcoming 2.0 billion Ecu-euro bond was expected to be launched this week, syndicate managers said on Monday.
The Spanish Treasury announced it was planning such a deal on April 10, saying it would surface between 15 and 30 days later. It said the issue would have a 10-year maturity.
Bankers said a mandate was likely to have been awarded, but it was as yet unclear which bank would underwrite the bond.

They said Spain had not yet decided on the exact maturity. The bond was expected to redenominate into the new single currency and become fungible with outstanding Spanish government bonds, bankers said.
"Spain is still undecided on the exact maturity," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.
"They may match the maturity with existing Bonos and make the deal fungible, in which case the maturity will be around 10.5 years," he said.
Spain was expected to pay in the mid- to high-10s basis points over the 5.5 percent April 2007 OAT benchmark, bankers said. At 1140 GMT this bond was quoted to yield 6.328 percent.
